scenes.animation: A classroom project day. Zippy's slide on the projector is crammed with tiny text in red on a purple background. The class squints; one student pulls out binoculars; the teacher's glasses fog up.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: I put my whole project on one slide. Why is nobody clapping?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Because nobody can read it. Let's learn what makes a presentation work.

scenes.animation: A definition card: 'Presentation = sharing ideas with an audience using a series of slides'. A stack of slides fans out, and a speaker cartoon points at them while an audience nods.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A presentation is a way of sharing information or ideas with an audience, using a series of slides.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Software like LibreOffice Impress helps you create these slides and show them on a screen.

scenes.animation: Icons pop onto a slide one at a time with labels: 'Text', 'Images', 'Audio', 'Video', 'Animation', 'Charts and tables'. Each icon does a small bounce as it lands.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The elements of a presentation are text, images, audio, video, animation, and charts or tables.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Text gives the key points. Pictures, sound and video make the message clear and interesting.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So I should add every sound effect and every spinning animation?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: No. Each element must help the message. Too many effects distract the audience.

scenes.animation: Zippy's messy slide is fixed live, with a tick appearing beside each rule: 'Short points, not paragraphs', 'Large readable font', 'Contrast: dark text on light background', 'Same design on every slide', 'Relevant pictures', 'Logical order: intro, body, conclusion'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: An effective presentation is simple. Use short points, not long paragraphs.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Use a large, readable font and colours with good contrast, like dark text on a light background.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Keep the same design on every slide, use relevant pictures, and follow a clear order from introduction to conclusion.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: And know your audience. A talk for Class 3 is different from one for the principal.

scenes.animation: A 'MINI PRACTICAL' card: '1. Take one crowded slide. 2. Cut it to 4 short points. 3. Fix the colours. 4. Add one relevant picture.' Then a yellow 'BOARD TIP' card: 'List 4 characteristics of a good presentation'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Try it: take one crowded slide, cut it down to four short points, fix the colours, and add one helpful picture.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: a common question asks for characteristics of an effective presentation. Simple, readable, consistent, and suited to the audience are safe points.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a projector icon. Points appear: '1. Presentation = ideas shared through slides', '2. Elements: text, images, audio, video, animation', '3. Keep it simple, readable, consistent, relevant'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: a presentation shares ideas with an audience through slides.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: its elements are text, images, audio, video and animation.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: a good presentation is simple, readable, consistent and relevant.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Binoculars returned. Applause received.

name: Starting LibreOffice Impress and Creating a Presentation

scenes.animation: Zippy stands before a school science fair judge with a cardboard chart that keeps flopping over. Neo flies in holding a laptop showing a neat slide titled 'Solar Energy'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: My chart paper keeps falling down. There has to be a better way!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: There is. LibreOffice Impress. Let's make your first presentation.

scenes.animation: Animated UI: in the LibreOffice Start Center, 'Impress Presentation' is clicked. A 'Select a Template' dialog opens with template thumbnails; one is chosen. Labels then pop onto the Impress window: 'Menu bar', 'Toolbars', 'Slides pane', 'Workspace', 'Sidebar', 'Status bar'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Open the Start Center and click Impress Presentation. A Select a Template box lets you start from a ready design, or close it for a blank one.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Older versions opened a Presentation Wizard here instead. Your textbook may show it.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The window has a menu bar and toolbars on top, the Slides pane on the left, the workspace in the middle, and the Sidebar on the right.

scenes.animation: The Sidebar's 'Layouts' panel is opened; thumbnails 'Title Slide', 'Title, Content', 'Title and 2 Content', 'Title Only', 'Blank Slide' glow. 'Title Slide' is clicked and the slide gets 'Click to add Title' and 'Click to add Text' boxes. 'Solar Energy' is typed in.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A slide layout decides where the title, text and pictures go. Pick one from the Layouts panel in the Sidebar, or from Slide, Layout.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Click the placeholder boxes and type your title and points.

scenes.animation: Key caps 'Ctrl+S' flash; the Save dialog shows 'SolarEnergy.odp'. Then key cap 'F5' starts a full-screen slide show; 'Esc' ends it. 'File > Export as PDF' creates 'SolarEnergy.pdf'. Finally 'File > Close' and 'Help > LibreOffice Help' with key cap 'F1' are shown.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Save with File, Save, or Control S. Impress saves as an O D P file.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Press F5 to run the slide show from the first slide. Press Escape to stop.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: What if the judge's computer doesn't have Impress?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Use File, Export as PDF. A PDF opens almost anywhere. Close the file with File, Close, and press F1 for Help.

scenes.animation: A 'MINI PRACTICAL' card: '1. Open Impress. 2. Choose a template. 3. Make a title slide. 4. Save, press F5, then export as PDF.' Then a yellow 'BOARD TIP' card: 'F5 = slide show · .odp = Impress file'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Try it: open Impress, choose a template, make a title slide, save it, run it with F5, and export a PDF.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: remember that F5 starts the slide show and that Impress files use the O D P extension.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a laptop icon. Points appear: '1. Impress window: Slides pane, workspace, Sidebar', '2. Template + layout to create slides', '3. Ctrl+S save, F5 show, File > Export as PDF'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: Impress has a Slides pane, a workspace and a Sidebar.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: start from a template and choose a layout for each slide.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: save with Control S, show with F5, and share as PDF.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Chart paper, you may finally rest.

scenes.animation: Zippy's presentation on Indian festivals has Diwali after Holi after Pongal in the wrong order. He tries to fix it by retyping each slide, sweating over a keyboard with smoke rising.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: My slides are in the wrong order. Do I have to type them all again?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Never. Impress lets you add, copy, move and delete whole slides in seconds.

scenes.animation: Animated UI: 'Slide > New Slide' with key caps 'Ctrl+M' adds a blank slide in the Slides pane. 'Slide > Duplicate Slide' creates an exact copy. The Layouts panel changes the new slide to 'Title, Content'. Right-click on a thumbnail shows 'Rename Slide' and 'Delete Slide'; the slide is renamed 'Diwali'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Add a slide with Slide, New Slide, or Control M. Slide, Duplicate Slide makes an exact copy.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Change its layout from the Layouts panel. Right-click a slide in the Slides pane to rename or delete it.

scenes.animation: In the Slides pane, the Diwali thumbnail is dragged to position 1 and the others shuffle down. Then a thumbnail is copied with 'Ctrl+C' and pasted with 'Ctrl+V'. On a slide, a text box is selected, copied, pasted, dragged to a new spot, then deleted with the Delete key.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: To move a slide, drag its thumbnail to a new place. To copy it, use copy and paste.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Contents work the same way. Select a text box or picture, then copy, cut, paste, drag or delete it.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So cut and paste moves it, and copy and paste clones it?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exactly right.

scenes.animation: The zoom slider in the status bar slides from 60% to 150%; 'View > Zoom' is also shown. Then the View menu opens and each view flashes on screen: 'Normal' (edit one slide), 'Outline' (all titles and points as text), 'Notes' (slide with speaker notes below), 'Slide Sorter' (grid of thumbnails).

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Zoom in or out with the slider on the status bar, or View, Zoom.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The View menu gives four workspace views. Normal is for editing one slide at a time.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Outline shows the titles and points of all slides as text. Notes lets you write speaker notes under each slide.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Slide Sorter shows every slide as a thumbnail, perfect for rearranging.

scenes.animation: A 'MINI PRACTICAL' card: '1. Make 4 festival slides with Ctrl+M. 2. Duplicate one. 3. Reorder in Slide Sorter. 4. Add notes in Notes view.' Then a yellow 'BOARD TIP' card: 'Slide Sorter = rearrange · Notes = speaker notes'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Try it: make four festival slides, duplicate one, put them in order in Slide Sorter, and add a speaker note.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: match each view to its use. Slide Sorter for arranging, Outline for text, Notes for speaker notes.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a shuffle-cards icon. Points appear: '1. Ctrl+M new slide; Duplicate, Rename, Delete', '2. Drag or copy/paste to move and copy', '3. Views: Normal, Outline, Notes, Slide Sorter'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: add, duplicate, rename and delete slides from the Slide menu or right-click.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: move and copy slides or contents by dragging or with copy and paste.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: use Normal, Outline, Notes and Slide Sorter views.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Diwali first. As it should be.

scenes.animation: Zippy's slide about the water cycle shows plain grey text all in one block. Then every word flies in from a different direction at once, colliding in the middle like dodgem cars.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: First it was boring, so I animated everything. Now it's a traffic jam!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Let's format the text neatly and animate only what matters.

scenes.animation: Animated UI: text is selected and the Formatting toolbar and Sidebar Character panel glow: font name, font size, Bold (Ctrl+B), Italic (Ctrl+I), Underline (Ctrl+U), font colour. Then alignment buttons with key caps: Left 'Ctrl+L', Centre 'Ctrl+E', Right 'Ctrl+R', Justified 'Ctrl+J'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Select the text first. Then use the Formatting toolbar or the Sidebar to change font, size and colour.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Bold is Control B, italic Control I, underline Control U.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Alignment can be left, centred, right or justified. Titles usually look best centred.

scenes.animation: Four lines 'Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, Collection' get bullets, then switch to '1. 2. 3. 4.' numbering using the toolbar toggles. 'Format > Bullets and Numbering' opens a dialog showing bullet shapes and number styles. Key caps 'Tab' and 'Shift+Tab' indent a point one level in and back out.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: For lists, use bullets or numbering from the toolbar. Numbers suit steps in order, like the water cycle.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Format, Bullets and Numbering lets you pick the bullet symbol or number style.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Press Tab at the start of a point to move it one level in, and Shift Tab to bring it back out.

scenes.animation: A cloud picture is selected. 'View > Animation' opens the Animation deck in the Sidebar. The '+' Add button is clicked; categories 'Entrance, Emphasis, Exit, Motion Paths, Misc Effects' appear; 'Entrance > Fly In' is chosen. Fields show 'Start: On click', 'Direction: From left', 'Duration'. A 'Play' preview runs.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Custom animation moves objects on a slide. Select the object and open the Animation deck in the Sidebar.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Click the Add button and choose a category, like entrance, emphasis or exit, and then an effect, like Fly In.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Set when it starts: on click, with previous, or after previous. You can also set its direction and duration.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So one smooth effect per point, not twelve!

scenes.animation: A 'MINI PRACTICAL' card: '1. Make a numbered water-cycle list. 2. Centre the title. 3. Add Fly In to the cloud, Start: On click. 4. Press Play.' Then a yellow 'BOARD TIP' card: 'Animation = objects on a slide · Transition = between slides'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Try it: make a numbered water-cycle list, centre the title, and give the cloud a Fly In entrance.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: do not mix up animation and transition. Animation moves objects on a slide. Transition is the effect between slides.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a raindrop icon. Points appear: '1. Formatting toolbar: font, size, bold, alignment', '2. Bullets and numbering for lists', '3. Animation deck: Add effect, set Start, direction, duration'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: format text with the Formatting toolbar and alignment buttons.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: use bullets or numbering for lists.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: add custom animation from the Animation deck and set how it starts.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Traffic jam cleared. The rain arrives on time.

scenes.animation: Zippy presents a slide on Indian states using long sentences with lots of spaces to line up numbers. The numbers wobble out of line, and a map he pasted appears upside down.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: My numbers won't line up, and my map is doing a headstand!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Use a table for the numbers and the image tools for the map.

scenes.animation: Animated UI: 'Insert > Table' opens the Insert Table dialog with 'Number of columns: 2', 'Number of rows: 4'. The table appears; 'State, Capital' is typed in the header, and the Tab key moves the cursor cell to cell: 'Kerala, Thiruvananthapuram', 'Punjab, Chandigarh', 'Assam, Dispur'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Choose Insert, Table, enter the number of columns and rows, and click OK.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Click a cell to type. Press Tab to jump to the next cell.

scenes.animation: Cells are selected by dragging: one cell, a whole row, a whole column. A column border is dragged to widen it; a row border is dragged to make it taller. The Table toolbar's Borders, Border Style and Area Style buttons, and 'Table Properties', add a border and a light blue background to the header row.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Drag across cells to select a cell, a row or a column. Drag a border line to change column width or row height.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Table toolbar appears when the table is selected. Use it, or Table Properties, to add borders and a background colour.

scenes.animation: 'Insert > Image' opens a file picker and a map image lands on the slide. Then the Sidebar's Gallery is opened and a clip-art arrow is dragged in. The map is dragged to move it, resized with a corner handle, and turned right side up with the rotation handles. The Image toolbar shows Filter, Colour, Transparency and Crop buttons.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Add a picture from your computer with Insert, Image, or drag one in from the Gallery in the Sidebar.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Drag the picture to move it, and drag a corner handle to resize it. Format, Position and Size lets you rotate it exactly.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: When an image is selected, the Image toolbar gives you filters, colour, transparency and cropping.

scenes.animation: From the Drawing toolbar a rectangle, a circle and an arrow line are drawn. They are selected together with Shift+click; 'Shape > Group > Group' with key caps 'Ctrl+Shift+G' joins them, and they move as one. 'Ungroup' separates them again. A 'MINI PRACTICAL' card and a yellow 'BOARD TIP' card follow.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Drawing toolbar adds lines and shapes. Select several shapes with Shift and click, then press Control Shift G to group them.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Grouped shapes move together, like a school trip in a line!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Try it: make a states table, add a map, and group three shapes into a label.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: grouping joins objects so they move and resize as one. Ungrouping separates them.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a table-and-picture icon. Points appear: '1. Insert > Table; Tab moves between cells', '2. Insert > Image or Gallery; move, resize, rotate', '3. Shapes from Drawing toolbar; group with Ctrl+Shift+G'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: insert tables, then format their size, borders and background.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: add images from a file or the Gallery, and move, resize or rotate them.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: draw lines and shapes and group them with Control Shift G.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Map right side up. India is relieved.

scenes.animation: Zippy has thirty slides and must add the school logo to each. He pastes it one slide at a time; by slide nine, logos are at different sizes and positions, like a wobbly sticker book.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Thirty slides, thirty logos, and none of them in the same place!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Put it on the slide master once, and every slide gets it.

scenes.animation: Animated UI: 'View > Master Slide' switches the workspace; a 'Master View' toolbar appears. The logo is placed in the top corner, the title font is changed to bold dark blue, and footer text 'Class 9 Project' is added. 'Close Master View' is clicked, and all thirty thumbnails update at once with a ripple effect.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A slide master is the template behind your slides. It holds the background, fonts, colours, logo and footer.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Choose View, Master Slide. Add the logo, change the title style, then click Close Master View.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Every slide using that master changes together. It saves time and keeps the design consistent.

scenes.animation: The Sidebar's 'Master Slides' panel shows 'Used in This Presentation' and 'Available for Use'. A different master is clicked and the selected slides take on its design.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Master Slides panel in the Sidebar shows the masters in use and others you can apply to your slides.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So the master is like the school uniform, and every slide wears it?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exactly. Same look, different content.

scenes.animation: 'Slide > Slide Transition' opens the Slide Transition deck in the Sidebar. Effect thumbnails 'Wipe, Fade, Push, Cover, Dissolve' appear; 'Fade' is chosen. Fields show 'Variant', 'Duration', 'Sound', and 'Advance Slide: On mouse click / Automatically after 5 sec'. 'Apply Transition to All Slides' is clicked, then 'Play' previews it.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A transition is the effect when one slide changes to the next. Choose Slide, Slide Transition, or open it in the Sidebar.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Pick an effect like Fade, set its duration, and add a sound if needed.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Under Advance Slide, choose on mouse click or automatically after some seconds. Click Apply Transition to All Slides for a matching show.

scenes.animation: A 'MINI PRACTICAL' card: '1. View > Master Slide: add a logo and footer. 2. Close Master View. 3. Add a Fade transition to all slides. 4. Press F5.' Then a yellow 'BOARD TIP' card: 'Master = common design for all slides'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Try it: add a logo and footer on the master, then apply one transition to all slides and run the show.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: if asked why we use a slide master, say it applies a common design to all slides at once.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a uniform-and-logo icon. Points appear: '1. Slide master = common background, fonts, logo', '2. View > Master Slide, then Close Master View', '3. Slide > Slide Transition: effect, duration, advance'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: a slide master gives all slides a common design.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: edit it with View, Master Slide, then close master view.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: transitions set how slides change, with effect, duration and advance options.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: One logo, thirty slides, zero wobble.
